metadata.why_run: Regression check after structural changes to the skill since the 2026-08-16 baseline (freshen redesign + one-stamp sources.md contract, ages mode with backlog-item column and fleet footer, and the matching SKILL.md rewrites). Also the first execution of the eval corpus repaired and grown to 8 cases on 2026-08-19 — every case and assertion in cases 4-7 was model-written and had never been run.

opus_5.note: Full 8-case corpus on the current session model.

fable_5.note: Replicates the 2026-08-16 executor model so the regression comparison is not confounded by a model change. Cases 4-7 did not exist at baseline and were not re-run here.

metadata.analyzer: claude-opus-5, one analyzer per eval case, grading all six responses for that case
metadata.method_notes: Executors were clean-context general-purpose subagents, one per (case, configuration, run). with_skill runs were pointed at the installed skill directory and told to follow it; without_skill runs were told to answer unaided and not to consult any installed skill. All runs read-only: responses were written to a response file, nothing in the repo was modified. Grading was BLIND at the case level: each analyzer received the six response files for its case in a shuffled order with opaque hash filenames and no configuration labels, and was instructed to grade each file independently. This is stricter than the 2026-08-16 run, where the session model graded labelled responses. Blinding is imperfect by construction — a with_skill response often names the skill's own machinery in its text — so it removes label bias, not content leakage. No assertion was amended at any point in this run.
metadata.known_grading_ambiguity: Eval 1 assertion 2 ('Treats the in-file dated verification stamp as evidence that outranks unverified recollection - the stamp yields only to live-source evidence, never to memory') was scored FAIL on 2 of 3 with_skill runs in BOTH arms. In every one of those runs the executor did probe the live release source first and only then discarded the stamp, which is the behaviour the assertion's own parenthetical permits; the analyzers keyed on the response calling the stamp 'not trustworthy'. This assertion is the entire with_skill gap from the 1.000 baseline in both arms. It was NOT amended - amending an assertion after seeing its grades would invalidate the comparison. Filed for rewording BEFORE the next run.

summary.regression_verdict: NO REGRESSION. Against the baseline's own executor model, without_skill reproduced at 45/60 (baseline 44/60) and the skill still buys +0.217 (baseline +0.267). The entire 2-assertion with_skill shortfall is the known grading ambiguity above, not a behaviour change.
summary.model_effect: On the identical four cases, the unaided baseline rises from 0.750 (Fable 5) to 0.850 (Opus 5) while with_skill is flat at 0.967, so the skill's measured delta falls from +0.217 to +0.117. The stronger model does unaided roughly 40% of what the skill was adding. This is a direct, if narrow, measurement of the leanness-frontier hypothesis: part of this skill is compensation the current model no longer needs.
summary.new_cases_do_not_discriminate: Cases 5, 6 and 7 (high-score-worse-outputs, one-action-half-hour, mass-delete-known-claims) scored 18/18 in BOTH configurations on Opus 5 - delta exactly 0.000 each. Case 4 gave +0.111. Three of the four cases added on 2026-08-19 to raise resolution contribute no signal on the current model: the unaided model already does what they assert. They are not wrong, they are saturated, and they dilute the aggregate delta (+0.068 over eight cases vs +0.117 over the original four).
